mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.label: Extreme pitch-speed distribution (probability of a 107+ mph pitch given pitcher max velocities and pitch counts)
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.measurement: For each pitcher: fit a generalized extreme value (GEV) or exponential tail to the pitcher's fastball speeds (top 1% of pitches) using the last 2 seasons; expected number of fastballs in the remaining window N_i; P(max_i >= 107) = 1 - exp(-N_i * P(speed >= 107 | fastball)). Combine across pitchers P(any) = 1 - Prod(1 - p_i). Include postseason pitches only for playoff teams. Units: probability. As-of: daily, with current-season maximum. CAVEATS: 107 mph lies beyond the observed record (about 105-106 mph tracked, unverified here), so an exponential tail fitted to the top 1% extrapolates; a physical-ceiling cap or generalised-Pareto fit with a finite endpoint is required. Independence across pitchers in P(any) = 1 - prod(1 - p_i) is an assumption (shared parks, radar calibration).
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.mechanism: The fastest pitch of a season is the maximum over pitches of a speed distribution with a heavy upper tail for a few pitchers.
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.rationale: A threshold of 107.0 mph is at the edge of the known distribution; the probability depends on a handful of pitchers' maximum fastball velocities, their usage and number of high-velocity pitches, and the tracking system measuring release speed.
raw_data: pitch-level release_speed for fastballs by pitcher; usage counts

mlb.mlbb_team_rating_series_format.label: Mobile Legends team rating (Elo/Glicko) and series-format win probability
mlb.mlbb_team_rating_series_format.measurement: Glicko-2 rating per team from map-level results (last 12 months, rating deviation decay), roster-change penalty (reset 30% of rating if >=2 starters change), patch-change variance inflation; match win probability from per-game win probability p and series format: best-of-3 P = p^2(3-2p), best-of-5 P = sum. As-of: at roster lock before the match. Units: probability.
mlb.mlbb_team_rating_series_format.mechanism: Match win probability depends on team strength and the best-of format that compresses or amplifies the gap.
mlb.mlbb_team_rating_series_format.rationale: KXMLBBGAME is not baseball; the relevant information is esports team strength, recent roster and patch changes, and map-level results (draft pick and ban), series length (best-of-3 or 5), and regional context.
raw_data: match-level: teams, map results, drafts, roster, patch, date

mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.label: Monthly/weekly window production rank (OPS, HR, ERA, K) within the award window
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.measurement: Rank players by composite score = z(wOBA or xwOBA) + z(HR) for hitters; z(ERA-) + z(K) for pitchers over the window (min PA/IP), using the final days before the selection date. Probability of selection from a logistic calibrated on 10 years of selection outcomes with features rank, team playoff odds, repeat winners. Units: probability. As-of: window end.
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.mechanism: Player of the Month/Week is chosen from production over a short window by a selection committee.
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.rationale: Short windows are noisy and the top performer in OPS or ERA is largely determined by luck, but the selection rule (batters from each league, pitchers separately) and narrative create structure.
raw_data: daily player stats for the window; award history

mlb.news_source_reliability_score.label: Source-level reliability: P(official | report type) from historical reports
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.measurement: For each reporter-source and wording class compute historical fraction of reports that led to the official event within 14 days (Beta posterior with prior from class average, k = 10 reports) and distribution of lead time. Output P(official by date) and expected lead. As-of: report timestamp. Units: probability and days.
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.mechanism: Not all reports are equal; some reporters' 'agreement reached' items are nearly always followed by official moves.
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.rationale: Market reaction to reports is only warranted if the posterior given the source and wording exceeds the market's pricing; track record and wording ('close', 'agreed', 'pending physical') strongly change completion probability.
raw_data: report-level: source, text, timestamp, outcome and official date

free_sources: MLB Stats API play-by-play (leverage, pitching changes)
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.label: Ninth-inning entry state (score margin, home-bats flag) and expected pitcher and due-up slots
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.measurement: P(home bats bottom 9) = P(home not leading after top 9) from the run distribution after 8 innings and top-9 runs. Margin entering 9 from simulated score distribution (innings 1-8). Pitcher: P(closer) = P(save situation: lead 1-3 for the home team entering visitor's top? (visitors pitching vs home)); for the visitor's top 9 the pitcher is the home team's closer if home leads by <=3, otherwise a setup/mop-up arm. Closer availability from usage in prior 2 days (back-to-back/3-in-4 flags). Due-up slots from expected PAs through eight innings (0-8 batters). Output: expected runs in top-9 and bottom-9 and P(any run). As-of: lineup post (prior) and live updates. WALK-OFF STOPPING RULE: bottom-9 (and later) runs are computed from a half-inning chain that terminates when the home team takes the lead. Tied entering the bottom: P(any run) = P(chain reaches a go-ahead run), and the run count is 1 unless the final hit is a home run (then 1 + runners on). Home trailing by d: only the first d+1 runs can score, again with the homer exception. This truncated distribution, not the untruncated half-inning run distribution, feeds KXMLBINNINGTOTAL over 1.5 and the Tie strike of KXMLBINNINGWIN.
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.mechanism: The 9th inning's run distribution depends on whether the home team bats, the margin, and who pitches.
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.rationale: KXMLBINNINGTOTAL and KXMLBINNINGWIN settle on the ninth only, including the case where the home team skips the bottom. The probability that the bottom of the ninth is played falls with home-team lead probability, and the pitcher is the closer in save situations or a mop-up arm in blowouts.
raw_data: inning-level: score diff entering 9, pitcher used, inning runs, closer usage history

mlb.offfield_base_rate.label: Reference-class base rate for non-game and business markets
mlb.offfield_base_rate.measurement: Compile historical frequency of the event type by window and season; adjust for current reports.
mlb.offfield_base_rate.mechanism: For off-field markets, history of similar announcements is the best available prior.
mlb.offfield_base_rate.rationale: No statistical model of on-field performance applies; probabilities depend on organisational decisions, calendars and reports. Subtle: resolution source defines what counts as official.

mlb.official_delay_record_definition.label: Minimum recorded delay duration and recording rule in official game data
mlb.official_delay_record_definition.measurement: From 5 seasons of MLB Stats API gamefeed and box-score notes: distribution of recorded delay duration; share of games with delay > 10, 30, 60 minutes; compare with weather-station precipitation timing at the park to estimate unrecorded stoppages (rain during play with no delay). Output P(recorded | rain in window) by duration bucket. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for completeness of recording. Units: probability.
mlb.official_delay_record_definition.mechanism: The contract counts any official weather delay; whether short stoppages are recorded determines what the data can verify.
mlb.official_delay_record_definition.rationale: If delays under about ten minutes are not recorded in the box score or play-by-play, history underestimates the event, and the question of whether a five-minute tarp pause counts is a contract question.
raw_data: game-level: delay start/end (if recorded), duration, reason, weather observations

mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.label: Scorer hit/error tendency by park (borderline play calls)
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.measurement: Per home park: hit-or-error ruling rate on batted balls with similar expected out probability (xBA bucket) vs league, over 3 seasons with k = 200 plays shrinkage; flag later rulings changes. Units: probability shift in hit given contact bucket. As-of: through prior game. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: scorer identity per game is not confirmed as a public pregame field. CAVEAT: no evidence is cited that scorer identity persists as a tendency; default to park-level hit/error rates and treat scorer identity as a hypothesis to test.
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.mechanism: Hits depend on official scorer rulings at the hit/error margin.
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.rationale: In some parks the scorer rules more plays errors than average, converting would-be hits into unearned reached-base events; changes made after the game may alter settlement values.
raw_data: play-level: batted ball class, official scoring result, park, scorer if available

mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.label: Confirmed opposing batting order out-rate profile: OBP, strikeout, ground-ball double-play and speed by slot against the starter's hand
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.measurement: For each of the nine confirmed slots take projected out probability per PA = 1 - OBP_proj(vs starter hand) + GIDP_rate x P(runner on first with <2 outs) (ZiPS/Steamer shrunk to 2-season stats with k = 300 PA), weighted by expected PA through the starter's modelled batters faced (slot PA weights 4.65 down to 3.85 per game, truncated to the starter's expected BF). Output: expected outs per batter faced for the lineup (about 0.68-0.72 league) and its deviation from league; units outs per BF. As-of: lineup post; before it, a mixture over the team's usual orders.
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.mechanism: Outs per batter faced depend on the nine specific hitters: on-base skill lowers outs per PA, strikeouts and grounders into double plays raise them.
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.rationale: The outs ladder converts batters faced into outs; a lineup of high-OBP, low-GIDP hitters can cost two or three outs over a start relative to a free-swinging lineup, and the order of the hitters changes who bats with runners on. The lineup posts a few hours before first pitch, so the input has a vintage problem.
raw_data: confirmed lineup with slots and handedness
hitter projection table by hand
PA events with outs on play and base state

mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.label: Outs per batter faced including double plays and baserunning outs
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.measurement: outs_per_BF = (1 - P(H) - P(BB) - P(HBP) - P(ROE) - P(FC reach)) + P(GIDP|BF) + (CS+PO outs)/BF. Compute pitcher-side P(GIDP) = P(GB) x P(runner on 1B, <2 out) x lineup DP rate (GIDP per opportunity of the confirmed batters, shrunk to league with k = 100 opportunities). Pitcher rates over 2 seasons half-life 300 BF, shrink k = 250 BF to league-by-handedness. Baserunning outs per BF from pickoff/CS counts with catcher arm and runner speed. Units: outs per batter. As-of: lineup post timestamp.
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.mechanism: Outs are not one per batter: GIDP adds a second out, and caught stealing and pickoffs add outs without a PA.
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.rationale: Using one minus OBP per batter understates outs for ground-ball pitchers with a double-play-prone lineup and a runner on first; it also ignores that reach-on-error and fielder's choice change who is out. This is the pitcher-level conversion that links batters faced to outs.
raw_data: event-level: batter, pitcher, events, outs_on_play, runners before, game state

mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.label: Leverage state: owners' revenue and broadcast contract position versus players' strike-fund and salary exposure
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.measurement: Construct a leverage ratio = owners' cost of lost games per week (national media revenue share + gate + local media at risk, from public estimates and league-wide revenue reports) divided by players' cost per week (average salary share of the schedule, with a distribution weighting by arbitration and minimum-salary players) and a strike-fund and reserve indicator for the union. Update quarterly; treat as ordinal (-1, 0, +1) when exact data is missing. As-of: latest annual report or credible estimate before the snapshot.
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.mechanism: A stoppage lasts as long as both sides' costs of waiting stay below their expected gain, which depends on revenue, television contracts, player earnings at risk and reserves.
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.rationale: Regional sports network disruptions, national TV renewals and a rising luxury tax change who loses more from lost games. A lockout is a bet that players, who miss paychecks, concede first. Those costs are observable only through proxies, so the input must be built from revenue indicators and public finance data.
raw_data: league revenue estimates and media contract terms
player payroll by tier, union reserves where disclosed

mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.label: Per-PA base-out state distribution from the confirmed lineup (Markov chain)
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.measurement: Build a nine-state-by-outs Markov chain for the confirmed lineup: transition probabilities per batter (P(1B), P(2B), P(HR), P(BB/HBP), P(K), P(GB DP), P(out other)) from batter true-talent shrunk to league with k = 200 PA and adjusted to the opposing starter and park. Run 10k simulated games or solve analytically to get P(runner on 1B, 2B, 3B; outs) at each of the hitter's PAs; summarise as expected runner-weighted opportunity (sum over runners aboard). Units: expected runners on base per PA. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.mechanism: RBI opportunity is the probability distribution of runners and outs when the hitter bats, derived from the hitters ahead.
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.rationale: Average RBI opportunity per slot hides lineup-specific variation: the same cleanup hitter has materially more RBI chances behind two .380-OBP hitters than behind two .300-OBP hitters, and opposing starter baserunner allowance scales it.
raw_data: PA-level events with base-out state; confirmed lineup and batter splits

mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.label: Expected PA split against the starter versus relievers with reliever handedness
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.measurement: From the hazard of starter exit (see pitcher archetypes) compute expected PA index at exit for each lineup slot; allocate remaining PAs to the likely bullpen sequence (closer excluded from innings before 9 unless lead is close) with reliever platoon shares by team/manager over last 2 seasons. Per-PA probabilities = batter splits vs the hand distribution; shrink batter-vs-hand splits to hitter overall with k = 200 PA vs same-hand and 400 PA vs opposite-hand. Units: expected PA vs starter, expected PA vs LHP relief, vs RHP relief. As-of: lineup post + bullpen availability.
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.mechanism: Later PAs are against relievers, often of the batter's weaker platoon side, so the hitter's per-PA rate differs for PA 1-3 versus 4-5.
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.rationale: Team-level bullpen talent hides which relievers the batter faces; the batter faces a distribution over reliever identities determined by starter exit time and managerial matchup use, which changes both handedness and quality.
raw_data: PA-level: batter, pitcher, pitcher hand, inning, role (starter or reliever), score state

mlb.park_specific_xhr.label: Park-and-weather-specific expected home runs per fly ball (xHR by batted-ball sector)
mlb.park_specific_xhr.measurement: From 4 seasons of batted balls with exit velocity, launch angle and spray angle, fit P(HR | EV, LA, spray) per park by logistic spline with park random effect; add wind component along the spray direction and air density as covariates. For each hitter compute expected HR per fly ball by integrating his empirical (EV, LA, spray) distribution (half-life 200 BIP, shrink to hand-class k = 150 BIP) over the game park with the day's wind and density. Units: probability per batted ball and per PA. As-of: forecast at lineup post.
mlb.park_specific_xhr.mechanism: Whether a hit fly ball clears the wall depends on distance, wall height in that sector, wind component, air density and roof.
mlb.park_specific_xhr.rationale: A park HR factor averages over all sprays; a pull-heavy hitter in a park with a short porch on his pull side gets a very different factor from a spray hitter. Deviation from the average on a specific day (wind out to right) matters most for hitters who hit to that sector.
raw_data: batted-ball: exit velocity, launch angle, spray, park, HR flag; weather: wind speed and direction, temperature, humidity, pressure; park geometry by sector

mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.label: Within-pitcher situational velocity lift: change in fastball speed with leverage, postseason, inning of appearance, pitch number, count, days of rest and temperature
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.measurement: Mixed model on fastball release_speed: pitcher random intercept and slope by season; fixed effects for leverage index bucket, postseason flag, pitch number within appearance (spline), two-strike count, days since last appearance (0,1,2,3+), game temperature (F) and roof closed; fit on 2021-2025 Statcast pitches; output per-situation additive lift in mph with standard errors, applied to each candidate's tail model.
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.mechanism: A pitcher's top speed on a given pitch is his baseline plus situational lifts; record pitches cluster in high-adrenaline, rested, warm, early-in-outing situations.
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.rationale: Velocity rises in the postseason and in high-leverage spots, falls after consecutive days of work and with pitch count, and is expected to be lower in colder air (effect size unverified, see velo_temperature_effect). Because the threshold sits in the extreme tail, a lift of half a mph multiplies the exceedance probability many times.
raw_data: pitch-level release_speed with game_pk, inning, pitch number, count, leverage proxy
game temperature and roof status
appearance dates

mlb.pitcher_gb_rate.label: Pitcher ground-ball rate and batted-ball mix
mlb.pitcher_gb_rate.measurement: GB%, FB%, LD%, pop-up% for pitcher, regressed; interact with lineup's launch-angle profile and team infield defence.
mlb.pitcher_gb_rate.mechanism: Ground-ball pitchers allow fewer HR and extra-base hits but more singles; batted-ball mix shapes hits, TB and double-play rates.
mlb.pitcher_gb_rate.rationale: GB% influences hits allowed vs TB and run scoring; for TB markets GB pitchers lower extra-base probability. Subtle: infield defence quality matters more for GB pitchers.

mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.label: Pitcher role and effort regime: starter pacing versus one-inning max-effort relief, and probability of a role change (including postseason bullpen use of starters)
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.measurement: Per candidate: current role (SP/RP/opener) and P(role change) over the remaining window from club statements and history; role-specific fastball speed distributions estimated from pitchers who switched role in 2015-2025 (within-pitcher difference in 99th-percentile speed, SP to RP, shrunk to the league mean shift). Output role-weighted tail parameters and exposure.
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.mechanism: Starters pace velocity over 90-100 pitches while one-inning relievers throw every pitch near peak, so the same arm reaches higher speeds in relief.
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.rationale: A hard-throwing starter typically sits 1.5-3 mph above his starting average when used in short relief. Postseason clubs often move starters to the bullpen, and clubs sometimes convert prospects to relief. The named-pitcher probability depends on which role he will occupy for how many appearances.
raw_data: appearance logs with role (start/relief) and innings
pitch-level speeds by appearance

mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.label: Starting-pitcher rotation slot, days of rest, off-day skipping and announced-probable status
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.measurement: For each pitcher compute (a) days_rest = game date - last start date, (b) expected next-start date = last start + 5 days adjusted for scheduled off days using the team's last 3 seasons of skip rate on off days (shrunk k = 20 team-off-days), (c) probable-pitcher announcement flag with timestamp and the historical change rate by days-to-game (own capture), (d) opener/bullpen-game rate of the team over the last 30 days. Output P(start on date d) = P(slot lands on d) x P(no change | announced). As-of: announcement time; before announcement the slot-based prior.
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.mechanism: A pitcher starts when his rotation turn arrives after the club's off days, injuries and bullpen days, and when the announced probable is not replaced.
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.rationale: KXMLBSTARTER-type markets depend on the rotation: position in the five-man (or six-man) order, days since the last start, whether the club will skip him around an off day, opener or bullpen-game usage, staff injuries and the probable-pitcher announcement vintage. Hitter lineup-card inputs (platoon, catcher rest, DH rotation) do not describe it.

mlb.player_involvement_mention_rate.label: Player and team name mention rate as a function of involvement (PA, pitching, storyline salience)
mlb.player_involvement_mention_rate.measurement: Model: mentions of player p per game = a_p x (PA_p + BF_p) + b_p x storyline_flag(p) with a_p estimated from 30+ transcribed games shrunk to role-class (star, regular, bench, pitcher) k = 10 games; storyline_flag from news on the previous 3 days (injury return, milestone, award talk). Zero when the player is not active. Units: mentions per game. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.player_involvement_mention_rate.mechanism: Names are said when players are in the action or in the news, in proportion to involvement.
mlb.player_involvement_mention_rate.rationale: A market on a specific player's name depends on whether he plays, bats in high-leverage spots, pitches, is injured or traded; base-rate tables for common baseball words do not apply.

mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.label: Playoff games played and plate-appearance distribution for a named player (for playoff-leader markets)
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.measurement: For each candidate: G_i = games in his team's remaining path from the bracket enumeration (distribution), PA per game by slot (4.3-4.6 for slots 1-3 falling to about 3.9), start probability from the lineup model; per-PA rate shrunk to projection (k = 300 PA). Simulate the stat count for each candidate over G_i and take the maximum; ties split per the contract. Output P(leader). As-of: daily.
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.mechanism: A playoff statistical leader needs games played, which depends on the team's bracket survival, and PA per game, which depends on lineup slot.
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.rationale: KXMLBLEADERPLAYOFF counts only playoff statistics and resolves No for non-participants, so the leader distribution is a maximum over players of a count over a random number of games; the games-played distribution comes from bracket survival and the PA share from lineup slot and rest.

mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.label: Playoff home-game allocation table: designated home team per game by round, seed and series length, with the as-played home log
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.measurement: Static table h(round, seed role, length): Wild Card Series best-of-3, higher seed (3 or 4) hosts every game (2 or 3), lower seed 0; Division Series 2-2-1, higher seed hosts G1, G2, G5 (2-3), lower seed G3, G4 (1-2); LCS 2-3-2 by seed and World Series 2-3-2 by regular-season record, higher seed hosts G1, G2, G6, G7 (2-4), lower seed G3-G5 (2-3). Combine with seed probabilities (mlb.season_sim, mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path) and series-length probabilities from the series model in the model layer, not here. As-of: format of the target season; per-game designated home team and venue logged after each game.
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.mechanism: Games hosted is a deterministic function of seed, rounds reached and series length through the format's home pattern; this input is that allocation rule plus the record of which club was the designated home team in each game already played.
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.rationale: The path convolution itself is a model output; the information needed is the allocation rule. It is easy to get wrong: a best-of-3 Wild Card Series is hosted entirely by seeds 3-4, so they can reach 13 hosted games, while bye seeds reach at most 11 and seeds 5-6 host nothing in round one. Designated home team, not venue, must be logged because relocation is possible.

mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.label: Playoff walk-off count: remaining-games exposure and per-game walk-off probability
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.measurement: Count so far W0 from official game results. Remaining games G are random: enumerate bracket paths and series lengths (best-of-5 or 7) from own per-game win probabilities. For each future game compute p_walkoff = P(home team trails by <=3 or is tied entering the bottom of the 9th and takes the lead before three outs, or wins in an extra inning) from the game run model plus half-inning chain with the visiting closer and due-up slots (walk-off stopping rule), shrunk to the league postseason rate over 2015-2025 with k = 100 games. P(count >= N) = P(W0 + sum Bernoulli(p_g) >= N) integrated over the distribution of G (Poisson-binomial mixture). Units: count and probability. As-of: daily during the playoffs.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.mechanism: A walk-off is a home-team win in the bottom of the 9th or an extra inning; the playoff count is the sum over remaining playoff games of a Bernoulli event whose probability depends on late-inning state, closer quality and who is home.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.rationale: KXMLBWALKOFFS pays on at least N walk-offs across the playoffs (the run that gives the home team the lead ends the game), so it is a count over a random number of games, with the count so far fixed. The per-game probability is not constant: it needs the home team to be tied or trailing by a small margin entering its last at-bat and to score the go-ahead run, and it varies with bullpen quality, extras probability and home-team identity.
raw_data: postseason game log with inning-by-inning score and walk-off flag

mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.label: Playoff-adjusted team rating (top-3 starters, top relievers, regular lineup) for short series
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.measurement: Rating = lineup wRC+ of the expected playoff nine (position players >= 70% of PA) + weights on top-3 starters (about 0.6 of innings in a series) using projection runs per 9 + top-4 relievers weights (about 0.3 of bullpen innings) minus bench contribution. Compute run differential per game with these weights vs the opponent; map to per-game win probability by logistic (0.1 per run). As-of: playoff roster and announced rotation. Units: expected run difference per game.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.mechanism: In October rotations shorten and top relievers pitch more, so the relevant team strength differs from the regular-season average.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.rationale: A team's regular-season run differential includes innings from fourth and fifth starters and mid bullpen arms that disappear in the playoffs; the weights shift toward the top of the rotation, top bullpen arms and starting lineup.
raw_data: player-level projections; playoff roster and rotation announcements

mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.label: League-wide playoff home-run count: games remaining by bracket path times per-game home-run expectation with game-level dispersion
mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.measurement: H0 = official playoff HR so far. For each remaining game g on each bracket path (probabilities from mlb.bracket_path_enumeration): lambda_g = sum over both teams of projected HR per PA (rest-of-season hitter projections vs the probable starter and bullpen, shrunk to team rate with k = 300 PA) x expected PA (about 38 per team) x park-and-weather factor (mlb.park_specific_xhr deciles). Game count ~ NB(lambda_g, phi) with phi from mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion. P(H0 + sum >= N) by Monte Carlo over paths and series lengths (20k draws). Calibrate total-HR-per-postseason predictions on 2015-2025 postseasons. Units: count and probability. As-of: after each playoff game.

mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.label: Starter removal hazard per batter faced (discrete-time survival curve)
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard h(b) = P(removed after batter b | still in) estimated on 5 seasons of starts (regular season; separate postseason intercept). Predictors: batters faced b (spline, knots at 9, 18, 27), pitch count (spline), runs allowed so far (0,1,2,3+), runners on at b, team lead/deficit bucket, days rest, season-to-date average pitches per start (shrunk to league with k = 8 starts), manager random effect (shrunk, k = 40 starts), bullpen-freshness index (relievers used last 2 days). Output: survival S(b) for b = 1..36 and E[BF]. As-of: manager and pitcher effects fit through the prior game; game-state predictors enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.mechanism: Batters faced is a first-passage time with removal hazard depending on pitch count, trip through the order, runs allowed and manager.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.rationale: The existing 'leash' label names the idea but gives no estimand. A K ladder cares about P(survive to batter 25+) and the hook is not a function of innings alone: a starter at 85 pitches with a 4-run deficit is removed at a different rate than one with a lead, and managers differ in whether they pull at the third-time-through boundary or at a pitch count. A measured hazard curve turns leash into a number the strikeout model can integrate over.

mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.label: Start-level dispersion of strikeouts beyond Poisson-binomial (rho parameter)
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.measurement: From 4 seasons of starts: for each start compute standardized residual of K given modelled expected K per batter faced (Pearson z = (K - sum p_i)/sqrt(sum p_i(1-p_i))). Estimate rho by moment matching: Var(K) = sum p_i(1-p_i) + rho*sum_{i!=j} sqrt(p_i(1-p_i)p_j(1-p_j)); pool pitchers by arsenal cluster (fastball-heavy, breaking-ball-heavy, finesse) and shrink to the pooled value with k = 25 starts. Report rho by cluster and by temperature bucket. As-of: estimated through the prior season, refreshed weekly in-season.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.mechanism: Strikeouts across the nine batters share a pitcher-day latent state, so counts are more dispersed than independent Bernoulli draws.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.rationale: The ladder prices neighbouring rungs from one distribution; if the variance is too small the 10+ and 11+ rungs are systematically underpriced and the 4+ rungs overpriced for high-K arms. A per-pitcher (or per-archetype) intra-start correlation parameter is the cheapest way to calibrate the width.
raw_data: start-level K, batters faced, per-batter expected K from the matchup model

For each batter: his own r2_b and c2_b, shrunk to league-by-hand with k = 150 PAs for r2 and k = 120 two-strike PAs for c2. Combine with odds-ratio (log5) per sub-event: logit(r2_match) = logit(r2_p) + logit(r2_b) - logit(r2_league), same for c2; matchup P(K) = r2_match * c2_match. Opposing hitters differ separately on 'gets to two strikes' (takes, fouls) and 'strikes out once there' (whiff on the chase pitch), so the matchup must be applied to each sub-event, not to the end rate.

mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.label: Team talent posterior (mean and standard deviation) combining projection prior and run differential
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.measurement: Prior mean mu0 = preseason projected win% (average of ZiPS/Steamer/PECOTA) with prior sd s0 = 0.04. Data: pythagenpat win% from RS/RA with n games and per-game outcome variance s_game^2 = 0.25 (binomial; use 0.22 for run-based). Conjugate normal update: weight on data w = n/(n + k) with k = s_game^2 / s0^2 = 0.25/0.0016 = about 156 games, so posterior mean = (1-w) mu0 + w pyth_wp and posterior variance = 1/(1/s0^2 + n/s_game^2); at n = 140 this gives sd of about 0.029 and at n = 162 about 0.028. Add roster shock: change in rest-of-season projected WAR per 162 games divided by 162 added to the mean, with variance 0.002 per shock. Units: win probability per game. As-of: daily after games.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.mechanism: True team strength is uncertain; its spread determines the width of win-total and title distributions.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A single rating hides that April uncertainty is large and that roster shocks widen it; futures prices at tails (95+ wins, a long-shot pennant) depend on the variance more than the mean.

mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.label: P(extra innings) from the inning-by-inning score chain, including tie-restoring bottom-9 halves
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.measurement: P(extras) = sum over states s of P(state s entering bottom 9) x P(home half-inning ends with score level), computed from an inning-by-inning Markov chain: states are (run differential after top 9, outs=0) with visitor closer PA rates (shrunk to league reliever rates, k = 150 BF) and home due-up hitters. Tied entering bottom 9: P(level) = P(home scores 0). Home trailing by d>=1: P(level) = P(home scores exactly d runs without taking the lead, the half ends on the third out). Home leading: no bottom 9, P(extras)=0. Walk-off stopping rule applied, so the half-inning ends once the home team takes the lead. Validate on 5 seasons by comparing predicted and observed extras rate by pre-game expected-total decile. Units: probability. As-of: confirmed lineups.
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.mechanism: Extras occur whenever the score is level after nine complete innings (or after the home half is played to its end), so the event is a function of the joint inning-by-inning chain, not of a single tied-entering-the-ninth conditional.
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.rationale: KXMLBEXTRAS pays when at least one extra inning is played. Games reach extras by two routes: tied after the top of the 9th with the home team failing to score, and visitors leading after the top of the 9th with the home team tying the score but not taking the lead (the half-inning ends on the third out, not on the tying run). Modelling only the first route understates P(extras); the home walk-off stopping rule also truncates the bottom-9 run distribution.

mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.label: Crew-specific word and phrase rate per broadcast hour with dispersion (transcript-based)
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.measurement: From transcripts (ASR with timestamps) of 40+ games per crew: for each word w count n_gw and exposure hours t_g; fit negative-binomial n_gw ~ NB(mean = t_g * lambda_cw, dispersion phi_cw) with lambda_cw shrunk to national lexeme rate with k = 6 games and phi pooled by word class. Stemming rules follow the contract text version. P(at least one) = 1 - integrated NB zero probability given expected exposure. As-of: before first pitch with crew known.
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.mechanism: Each crew has a characteristic per-hour rate for each lexeme and a dispersion beyond Poisson.
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.rationale: The catalog's mention_text names crew language tendencies without a measurement; the question needs per-word per-crew rates and a dispersion estimate because probability of at least one is concave in the rate and depends on clustering.
